income.name: Colombia

income_tax.summary: Colombian fiscal residents (183 days in any 365) are taxed on worldwide income at progressive rates from 0% to 39% (thresholds in UVT, UVT = COP 52,347 for 2026). Employees pay 4% health and 4% pension (plus solidarity surcharges); independents contribute 12.5% health and 16% pension on a base of 40% of income, capped at 25 minimum wages.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Independents with service contracts contribute on an IBC of 40% of monthly income (floor one minimum wage COP 1,750,905, ceiling 25 minimum wages COP 43,772,625): health 12.5% + pension 16% = 28.5% of IBC, i.e. an effective 11.4% of gross income (ARL occupational-risk cover is also due for contracts over a month; solidarity-fund surcharge of 1% above 4 minimum wages not added). The cap is expressed on gross income (IBC cap / 0.4).
income_tax.local_tax_note: No municipal surtax on personal income (Medellin levies industry-and-commerce tax on business activity, not modelled).

regimes.name: Visa V - Digital nomad
regimes.description: Colombian digital nomad visa for remote workers paid from abroad. Requires regular foreign-source income of at least three monthly minimum wages for the previous three months, health insurance, and no work for Colombian employers or clients. It does not change tax: after more than 183 days in a 365-day period the holder is a fiscal resident taxed on worldwide income.
regimes.duration_note: Valid up to 24 months from issue per the cited guide; renewal not addressed by the source.

Renewal rules and social security for visa holders not stated by the source; social_security_applies is True only for residents who contribute as independents/employees locally.

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other visa-exempt nationalities can stay as tourists (up to 180 days a year) without working locally. Remote workers can apply for the Visa V digital nomad visa (foreign income of at least three minimum wages, health insurance), which does not lead to permanent residence by itself. Skilled employees of a Colombian employer need a work visa (Visa M) sponsored by the employer; other visa routes (partner, investor, Mercosur-style agreements for some nationalities) exist but were not researched.
open_questions: Official Cancilleria page for Visa V was not reached; income and duration come from a guide.
Rent (2-bedroom): value is the lower end of a published El Poblado range, not a sample median.
